questions.question:
**Select the alternative that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case there is no improvement select ‘No improvement’.**

Sidharth __want to become__ a football player but needs to practice more rigorously.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is - **wants to become**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The simple present tense is used when an action is happening right now, to state or ask about things in general, or when it happens regularly or unceasingly.
 
• The structure is given below:
 
 
• Subject + V1 + object.
 
 
 
• The verb will take 's/es' if the given noun/pronoun (3rd person) is singular.
 
• Example:
 
 
• *​He plays badminton daily.​*
 
 
 
• Certain verbs used only in the simple present tense are given below:
 
 
• ​verbs of perception (see, hear, smell, etc.), think, know, has/have, possess, like, want, desire, hate, seem, imagine, etc.
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *​My brother is owning a car. (incorrect)*
 
• *​My brother owns a car. (correct)*
 
 
 
• As per the rules given above, the **2nd option i.e. wants to become** is the correct choice.

 

Correct Sentence__: *Sidharth **wants to become** a football player but needs to practice more rigorously.*

The Director will __agree with the proposal__ if we do not exceed the budget.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**agree to the proposal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agree to something: **to accept someone else’s plan, suggestion, etc

 **Example: **Often promoters will try to get people to agree to a deal.
 
• **Agree with** means to have the same opinion as another person or to approve of something.

 **Example: **I agree with you that spaghetti sauce can never have too much garlic.
 
• **Agree on** means to share the same opinion about items, topics, or standards

 **Example: **All parties agreed on plans to expand the Rideau Centre.
 
• The proposal is a kind of suggestion/ plan, **agree to **will be suitable

**Thus, the improved sentence is:** *The Director will **agree to the proposal__** if we do not exceed the budget.*

Of the two plans submitted by the architect, this is the one __more likely__ to be accepted.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'No substitution required'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically correct.
 
• The given sentence is talking about the** two plans** submitted by the architect.
 
• When the **comparison** is being made between **two things **we use the** comparative degree **instead of the** superlative degree.**
 
• Hence, in the given sentence '**more**' is correctly used.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *Of the two plans submitted by the architect, this is the one **more likely** to be accepted.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

Our microwave oven is out of order and __repairing is needed for it.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- 'needs to be repaired.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the *conjunction *'**and**' joins two clauses of the **same degree **and **importance**.
 
• As the first clause is in **present indefinite tense **so the second sentence should **also **be in **present indefinite tense**.
 
• For a **singular subject **(*microwave oven*) a **singular verb **(*needs*) should be used.
 
• Thus ***option 3 ***is the correct answer.

**And the correct sentence is: ***Our microwave oven is out of order and **needs to be repaired **for it*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Let's learn the use of various conjunctions:

 
 
• Coordinating Conjunctions: They join like with like. In other words, they join a noun with another noun or an adjective with another adjective. There are seven in total: *for, and, nor, but, or, yet, *and *so*.

 
 
• Example: *He was late for school, so he took a shortcut.*
 
 
 
• Subordinating Conjunctions: They join *subordinate clauses *to *main clauses*. Common examples are *although, because, if, since, unless, until,* and *while*.
 
 
• Example: *Because it was raining (main clause), we had to cancel the class picnic (subordinate clause).*
 
 
 
• Correlative Conjunctions: They are used in pairs to join alternatives or equal elements. The most common pairs are *either...or, neither...nor, *and *not only...but also.*
 
 
• *​*Example: *You can have either chocolate or vanilla ice cream.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

India __have a man__y all-rounders to match the talent and dedication of Kapil Dev.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'has few'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
 
• The erroneous part **'have a many' **should be **'has few'. **
 
• The given sentence has** two errors. **
 
• Firstly, 'has' should be used instead of **'have'** because **'India'** is singular. Therefore, **a singular helping verb** should be used. 
 
• The given sentence is talking about the lack of all-rounders in the Indian team. 
 
• The word **'a many'** refers to a large number of **something countable.** Therefore, the use of **''a many''** is grammatically incorrect. 
 
• The word **'few'** has **a negative meaning.** We use them to mean **‘not as much as may be expected or wished for.'**
 
• We use few with **plural countable nouns. **
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *India **has few** all-rounders to match the talent and dedication of Kapil Dev.* 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **"A little"** and **"a few"** are quantifiers meaning** ‘some’.** **"Little **and **few" **have negative meanings. We use them to mean **‘not as much as may be expected or wished for’. **
 
• Their Comparision as follows: 
 
 
• 
 
 
 

 *All she wanted was **a few** moments on her own.*
 **some, a small number**
 
 

 *She had **few **moments on her own.*
 **not many/almost none**
 
 

 *She saves **a little** money every month.*
 **some, a small amount**
 
 

 *They had **little **money to spend.*
 **not much/almost nothing**
 
 

 
 
*A: Have you got any money?*

 
*B: Yes,** a little.***

 
 **some, a small amount**
 
 

 
 
*A: Have you got any money?*

 
*B: No, very **little**.*

 
 **not much/almost nothing**
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• **A little, a few with a noun**
 
 
• We use **"a little"** with singular **uncountable nouns.** We use **"a few"** with **plural countable nouns.** 
 
• Examples: 
 
 
• *Mary said nothing, but she drank some tea and ate **a little **bread.*
 
• *We stayed** a few** days in Florence and visited the museums.*
 
 
 
 
 
• **Little, few with a noun**
 
 
• We use **"little"** with **uncountable nouns.** We use** "few"** with **plural countable nouns.** They are used in formal contexts. 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *I’m not very happy about it but I suppose I have **little **choice.*
 
• ***Few **cities anywhere in Europe can match the cultural richness of Berlin.*

The student __apologised the teache__r for the delay in submitting the assignment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'apologised to the teacher'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part in the given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'apologised to the teacher' **should be used instead of** 'apologised the teacher'.**
 
• The verb '**apologise**' should be followed by the **preposition** '**to**' in the given context. 
 
• It means 'to say that you are sorry for something that you have done'. [(किसी से) (किसी बात के लिए) क्षमा याचना करना]
 
 
• *Example: You’ll have to **apologise to** your teacher for being late.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *The student **apologised to the teacher** for the delay in submitting the assignment.*

The first meeting of the Standing Committee __will be hold next week.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'will be held next week'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'will be held next week'** should be used instead of** 'will be hold next week'.**
 
• We know that after '**will + be**' **past participle form** of the **verb**(**held**) is used as the sentence is in passive voice.
 
 
• *Example: He **will be brought** home tomorrow.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *The first meeting of the Standing Committee **will be held next week.***** **

A tigress __has given birth__ to a cub in the Ranthambore Tiger Reserve, taking the big cat population to 78.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'no substitution required'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically correct.
 
• In the given sentence** 'A tigress' **is **a singular subject.**
 
• Hence, **a singular auxiliary verb** '**has**' is used.
 
• We know that '**has**' is followed by the **'past participle'. **In the given sentence **'given' **is the **past participle** of the **verb** '**give**'.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *A tigress **has given birth** to a cub in the Ranthambore Tiger Reserve, taking the big cat population to 78. *

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.**

It is reported that everyday __India witnessing the death__ of over 2000 babies aged less than one year.

options.text: India will be witness the death

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**India witnesses the death**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the **present participle** form of the verb 'witnessing' used is incorrect.
 
• The verb third-person singular present should be used with the noun 'India'.
 
• Therefore, the third-person singular verb 'witnesses' should be used instead of the present participle form of the verb '**witnessing**'.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

 

Correct Sentence__: *It is reported that everyday **India witnesses the death** of over 2000 babies aged less than one year.*
